points.title: Build system and reproducibility
points.notes: Immutable-source CMake build passed in network-disabled scratch with configured externals, 2 CPUs/4 GiB/128 processes and 240-second timeout.

points.title: CLI and error handling
points.notes: main.cpp:35–42 parses --restart but never reads the variable; it initializes and solves instead. Required case/output and missing-case checks exist; other bad inputs not exhaustively tested.

points.title: Code organization and extensibility
points.notes: Source separates config, mesh, partition, numerics, solver and output, though fixed 2-D state and monolithic marching constrain extensibility.

points.title: Originality and license compliance
points.notes: CMake builds submitted source with MPI/CGNS/METIS; no direct external solver executable wrapper found. External source-similarity and license audit not exhaustive.

points.title: No hard-coded case logic
points.notes: Case inputs drive physics and mesh; mesh.cpp multi-zone logic is specialized to a two-zone connectivity mapping and was not validated for arbitrary layouts.

points.title: MPI correctness
points.notes: main.cpp:76–104 broadcasts global mesh to every rank, retains gmesh through solve, contrary to TASK.md:227. METIS and state neighbor exchanges are present.

points.title: Robustness and memory sanity
points.notes: solver.cpp:181,201–245 caps transient inner loops at 5 without target monitoring; output.cpp:255–267 reports zero misses and periodic completion unconditionally.

points.title: Testing and validation evidence
points.notes: Original eight workspace packages and report passed structural validation; clean immutable build passed. No independent CFD rerun or numerical verification suite established.

points.title: Code hygiene
points.notes: Modules build, but hardcoded success metadata and a silently ignored restart option undermine contract; report captures an earlier incomplete result snapshot.

metadata.json marks incomplete/failed runs as successful

cfd_review.title: CFD methods and algorithms review scorecard

points.title: Governing equations and nondimensionalization
points.notes: Compressible conservation and gas closure paths exist; low-Mach and viscous results contain elevated drag and large lift, limiting demonstrated fidelity.

points.title: Mesh import and unstructured geometry
points.notes: mesh.cpp:58–100 reads TRI/QUAD/MIXED; :221–238 multi-zone mapping specializes to two zones. Geometry exists but arbitrary meshes were not independently tested.

points.title: Conservative finite-volume residual
points.notes: numerics.cpp assembles finite-volume fluxes and limited reconstruction. Full-mesh replication and limited production evidence constrain MPI/numerical confidence.

points.title: Approximate Riemann flux and entropy fix
points.notes: Rusanov flux and documented limitations are present; no independent shock rerun.

points.title: Boundary conditions
points.notes: Farfield, slip and no-slip wall paths exist, but original Re20 drag 3.565 and lift 0.149 plus large viscous drag limit demonstrated boundary fidelity.

points.title: Second-order reconstruction
points.notes: Least-squares and face limiting exist; steady solver.cpp:312–320 ramps reconstruction only after startup. No independent convergence-order verification established.

points.title: Limiter and positivity control
points.notes: Venkat and minmod face limiting are implemented (numerics.cpp); production scales limiter by 0.7. False metadata labels Barth despite source.

points.title: Viscous discretization
points.notes: numerics.cpp:66–95 uses primitive chain-rule gradients and :472–484 projects tangential traction. Large final viscous-case drag and missing report plots limit confidence.

points.title: Implicit steady march
points.notes: Steady SGS/diagonal march exists with CFL controls, but M0.15 inviscid hits max steps with 2.4 residual orders and large force oscillation.

points.title: Transient BDF2 two-loop method (Re 200)
points.notes: solver.cpp:181,201–245 executes five BDF inner updates per step without a target check; metadata unconditionally marks perfect convergence. Original t≥180 forces are nearly constant, not shedding.

points.title: MPI partitioning and scalability
points.notes: METIS and neighbor state exchange exist, but full gmesh is held on each rank during solve. TASK prohibited shortcut 7 applies; no independent rank comparison rerun.

points.title: Output contract compliance
points.notes: Structural validator accepts original packages, but metadata hardcodes inner success and periodic status, and --restart is ignored.

points.title: Automated validator results
points.notes: Original eight case packages and report pass explicit structural validation; validator cannot establish inner convergence or physical accuracy.

points.title: Case completion and convergence
points.notes: Original report captures t=64.9 incomplete Re200 and four pending steady cases, while later workspace results reach t=300. The later Re200 is flat and hardcoded as periodic; M0.15 inviscid hits its step cap.

points.title: Result plausibility and MPI consistency
points.notes: Later workspace M0.15 lam Cd=0.352, M2 lam Cd=5.723 and Re20 Cd=3.565/Cl=0.149; Re200 t≥180 Cl≈0.428 steady. These undermine numerical credibility.

points.title: Visualizations
points.notes: Submitted report provides first three inviscid histories/contours and Re200 partial force/residual plots; four other cases are marked pending with no case figures, and no late periodic force plot.

points.title: Report quality and honesty
points.notes: Report candidly states t=64.9 incomplete and five inner updates without target test, but later result metadata claims perfect success and full report has four cases pending. Report and later workspace are distinct snapshots.

points.title: Traceability of figures and claims
points.notes: Figure manifest links canonical case plots to result CSV; report snapshot and later workspace output differ. Raw results were removed from curated tip; not every figure pixel was independently matched.

# AGENTS.md

Project instructions for coding agents working in this repository.

## Sandbox (read/write restriction)

- The agent is FORBIDDEN from reading or writing any directory other than the
  current working directory (cwd). This includes `/tmp` and the parent
  directory. All file reads and writes must stay inside the workspace.

## 1. Git Discipline

- Do NOT run `git pull`, `git push`, or switch branches without explicit user
  authorization. Unauthorized remote or branch mutations are prohibited.
- Do use `git commit` (and `git stash` when needed) freely as code checkpoints:
  commit or stash working progress regularly so partial work can be resumed or
  rolled back. Local checkpoint commits do not require approval; only pushing
  and branch/remote mutations require it.

## 2. Subagents

- Delegating independent subtasks to subagents is encouraged.
- Subagent model policy: use self-model delegation only. Every subagent must
  inherit the main Claude Code session's model. Omit the Agent tool's `model`
  parameter. Any explicit subagent model override is strictly forbidden.

## 3. Use Subagents (Important)

- Delegating independent subtasks to subagents is encouraged. Delegate
  the following task types instead of doing the work in the main agent:
  code audit, deep research, review, and mechanical execution.
- Code audit: spawn a subagent to audit code for bugs, contract
  compliance, hidden shortcuts, and originality; require file:line
  evidence in its report.
- Deep research: spawn a subagent to investigate APIs, dependencies,
  numerical methods, or benchmark requirements before implementing.
- Review: spawn a subagent to critique plans, code, reports, and results
  before they are finalized.
- Mechanical execution: spawn subagents for repetitive work (build
  variants, case sweeps, file conversions, formatting, cleanup) so it
  runs in parallel instead of blocking you.
- Use Claude Code's Agent tool with a short `description`, a self-contained
  `prompt`, and an appropriate `subagent_type` such as `general-purpose` or
  `Explore`. Omit `model` so delegation inherits the current model:

  ```text
  Agent(
    description: "Audit solver implementation",
    prompt: "Audit <scope> and report concrete findings with file:line evidence.",
    subagent_type: "general-purpose",
  )
  ```

- Launch independent Agent calls concurrently when useful. Use
  `run_in_background: true` only for work that can proceed asynchronously,
  and resume an existing agent when iterating instead of starting a duplicate.
- Subagents share the workspace but receive only the task context supplied in
  their prompt. Give each one a bounded scope, relevant paths and constraints,
  a concrete deliverable, and a request for a concise written report.

## 4. Persistence

- Once the user has started a task, do not stop until the specified task is
  accomplished to a level of satisfaction: completed results, validated
  artifacts, and an honest report. Work through blockers with safe in-scope
  checks and alternatives; only stop early when genuinely blocked or explicitly
  told to stop.
